role.altitude: The controller spends less time collecting data and checking routine invoices. They own the rule set that machines run (approval matrix, tie-out checks, materiality thresholds, accrual handbook) and they decide the exceptions those rules send to them.
reach: FP&A Analyst: plan-to-forecast driver models, to link margin findings to the rolling forecast
Bookkeeper (accounts payable): invoice coding and matching, to tune disbursement checks where false alarms come from
Payroll Specialist: WKR (werkkostenregeling) postings, to bring the WKR free space into tax planning
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: the AFAS extract and Power BI model, to share one governed data layer with HR
skills_to_grow: Writing control rules as testable specifications instead of prose procedures
Enough SQL to read and change a check or tie-out query on the data platform
Reviewing model-drafted commentary and memos critically: sources, confident errors
Audit trail design: what the external auditor needs to rebuild an approval or estimate
role.ambitious_version: A margin and cost-leak review per site, customer and staffing agency that is ready two days after close every month, and a payment gate where no Rabobank batch leaves unless the budget, contract, duplicate and IBAN-change checks passed or the controller signed off the exception. Both feed the North Star: fewer days to close, fewer audit adjustments.

tasks.short: Analyse past, current and expected results per site and customer to find improvements and weak spots.

steps.what: Pull ledger, cost-centre and flex-hour data into Excel
Build variance and margin views per site, customer and agency
Find drivers and outliers and write first explanations

loop.input: variances above threshold with their top journal lines, invoice texts and prior-month commentary
loop.output: short driver explanation per variance with the journal lines it rests on
loop.check: every amount quoted must match the ledger query; explanations without a cited journal line are dropped
loop.stop: one pass per variance above threshold, max 40 per month; no explanation found means 'unexplained' for the controller
loop.why_not_simpler: the reason sits in free-text invoice and journal descriptions, which fixed rules cannot summarise

steps.what: Judge which improvement opportunities are real and size them
Write the management memo

loop.input: improvement shortlist with figures and controller notes
loop.output: memo draft in the house template
loop.check: figures pulled from the dashboard by reference, not retyped; controller edits and signs
loop.stop: one draft plus one revision on request; otherwise controller writes
loop.why_not_simpler: a template fills figures but cannot write the argument in plain prose

steps.what: Discuss findings with finance director and site managers

tasks.design: Replace the monthly Excel pull with a scheduled Python job on a governed data platform that reads AFAS GetConnectors and the agency portal exports, and feeds a Power BI margin and variance dashboard per site, customer and agency. A bounded model step drafts driver commentary for variances above threshold, citing journal lines; the controller judges, edits the memo draft and discusses actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data sat in three places (AFAS, agency portals, Power BI extract) and joining them took manual Excel work each month; commentary needed someone to read journal texts.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the extract-and-join jobs cheap to build, and current models can write grounded first-draft variance commentary from journal lines.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding which variance points to a real improvement, and getting site managers to act on it; agency data quality varies.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the operations behind the numbers (a lost customer, a seasonal peak, a site manager's habits) and persuading people to change.

ambition.what: A monthly margin and flex-cost review per site and customer instead of an occasional ad-hoc analysis

tasks.altitude: The controller stops building workbooks and spends the time on two or three findings per month with site managers. They gain the right to set the variance thresholds that trigger a review.

reach.learn: How drivers found in actuals feed forecast assumptions
Where flex-cost data is incomplete or late

evidence.claim: AI-using accountants closed the month 7.5 days faster across 79 small and mid-sized firms
On full close tasks the bottleneck is accounting judgement, not retrieval
AFAS Profit exposes data through GetConnectors usable by scheduled jobs

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract behind Power BI can be reused or extended
Agency portals offer exportable hour and invoice data
No personal data beyond agency worker hours per cost centre is needed, so no works council consent applies
unknowns: How often the controller does this analysis today and for whom
Whether customer-level margin can be built from AFAS cost centres and projects
Which agency portals have an export or API
research_questions: Can customer and site margin be computed from AFAS data without manual allocation keys?
Do site managers act on a monthly review, or is quarterly enough?
How often do drafted variance explanations match what the controller would write, on three past months?

tasks.short: Write and update internal control policies and procedures for budget, cash, credit and accounting.

steps.what: Collect audit findings, incidents and current policies

loop.input: auditor management letter, incident mails, current SharePoint policies
loop.output: list of findings mapped to the policy section they touch
loop.check: each item links to its source passage; controller confirms the list
loop.stop: one pass per document; unmapped findings listed as 'no section'
loop.why_not_simpler: findings are free text in letters and mails

steps.what: Draft or revise policy and procedure text

loop.input: policy gap list, existing policy, controller instructions
loop.check: controller reviews every change; thresholds and limits only from the approval matrix, never invented
loop.stop: two revision rounds, then controller edits by hand
loop.why_not_simpler: prose procedures need writing, not a fill-in template

steps.what: Check AFAS approval limits and segregation of duties against policy
Consult finance director, accountants and bookkeepers
Approve, publish, configure AFAS and track staff acknowledgement

tasks.design: Keep policies on SharePoint but add a Power Automate approval and acknowledgement flow, and a deterministic check on the data platform that compares AFAS authorisation and approval-limit settings against the approval matrix. A bounded model step extracts findings from management letters and drafts tracked-changes revisions for the controller to edit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy work is occasional, text-heavy and tied to judgement, so it never justified tooling; AFAS settings were checked by hand on screen.
tasks.enabler_now: Models draft procedure text and map audit findings to sections reliably enough for review; a settings-versus-policy check is quick to build.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the right control level for a 1,200-person company with seasonal flex volume, and getting people to follow it.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing control strength against workload in the team, and agreeing it with the finance director and auditor.

ambition.what: A monthly check that AFAS approval limits and segregation of duties still match the approval matrix

tasks.altitude: Less drafting time; the controller decides the control level and owns the approval matrix as a maintained record instead of a document.

reach.learn: Which controls slow the close without catching errors
Where the credit policy is bent in practice

evidence.claim: Tax and cash decisions need mandatory human review with timestamped logs
Estimates kept in personal AI accounts cannot be rebuilt by the auditor
SharePoint with Power Automate supports approval and read-acknowledgement flows

assumptions: AFAS authorisation settings can be exported or read via API
Acknowledgement tracking logs staff names, which may need a short works council check if used to monitor behaviour
unknowns: Whether an approval matrix exists as a single document
How many control findings the auditor raised last year
research_questions: Can AFAS role and approval-limit settings be read by API for an automated comparison?
Did last year's management letter contain findings a settings check would have caught?
Does the auditor accept model-drafted procedures if the controller signs them?

tasks.short: Plan corporate tax, VAT and investment deductions with the tax advisor.

steps.what: Extract trial balance, fixed assets and WKR costs
Compute expected corporate tax and provisional assessment position
Spot planning options: EIA/MIA on investments, WKR space, timing

loop.input: new investment and purchase invoice descriptions
loop.output: candidate EIA/MIA/KIA flags with the list item they may match
loop.check: controller and tax advisor confirm each flag; amounts from AFAS only
loop.stop: one pass per new asset line monthly; low-confidence lines listed as 'check'
loop.why_not_simpler: asset descriptions are free text that fixed codes do not cover

steps.what: Discuss options with external tax advisor and decide
Have advisor file notifications or adjust provisional assessment

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the data platform builds the tax data pack from AFAS and a deterministic workbook computes the expected corporate tax and WKR use. A bounded model step flags new investments that may qualify for EIA/MIA/KIA, and a deadline notification warns before the EIA notification window closes; the controller and advisor decide and the advisor files.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tax planning is yearly, low volume and judgement-heavy, so nobody built tooling; investment eligibility needed someone reading invoice texts.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap-to-build data jobs and models that classify free-text asset lines with a cited match for review.
tasks.still_hard: Tax judgement, interpretation of Dutch rules and liability stay with the advisor and the controller; models are untested on Dutch tax.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing tax risk against cash and business plans, and the relationship with the advisor and the Belastingdienst.

ambition.what: A monthly check of new investments against EIA/MIA deadlines instead of a year-end search

tasks.altitude: Less spreadsheet work; the controller reviews flags monthly and brings fewer, better-prepared questions to the advisor.

reach.learn: How much of the free space is used during the year
Which planned investments could qualify for deductions

evidence.claim: Tax estimates need mandatory human review and approval with timestamped logs
Close benchmarks are US GAAP; Dutch tax is untested
EIA must be notified within three months of the investment commitment

assumptions: An external tax advisor prepares and files the returns
Investments in electric trucks, warehouse lighting or solar happen often enough to matter
The fixed asset register is kept in AFAS
unknowns: Whether EIA/MIA opportunities were missed in recent years
Who files the WKR final levy and how it is tracked
How the advisor charges for planning work
research_questions: How many investments in the last two years qualified for EIA/MIA and were they all notified in time?
Can the model flags be checked against the advisor's past classifications with good agreement?
Does the advisor accept a structured tax data pack instead of their own request list?

tasks.short: Receive, check and approve payment requests and authorise payment batches.

steps.what: Receive requests by mail and AFAS workflow, record stragglers
Check budget, contract, PO, duplicates and IBAN changes
Match agency invoices to approved flex hours

loop.input: agency invoice PDFs that arrive without structured data
loop.output: invoice lines (worker, week, hours, rate) for the deterministic match
loop.check: line totals must add up to the invoice total; hours matched to portal export within zero tolerance
loop.stop: one extraction per invoice; mismatch or failed total goes to the bookkeeper queue
loop.why_not_simpler: not all three agencies send UBL or structured exports

steps.what: Judge exceptions and approve above threshold
Authorise payment batch in Rabobank

tasks.design: Close the mail route so every request enters the AFAS purchase invoice workflow, and run deterministic checks (budget, contract, PO, duplicate, IBAN change) as a scheduled job on the data platform that writes a pass or exception flag back to AFAS. Agency invoices are matched to portal hours, with a bounded extraction step only for PDF invoices; the controller approves exceptions and large amounts and signs the Rabobank batch with a summary of what passed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived through several channels and agency invoices came in different formats, so checks were done by eye in AFAS and Excel.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS workflows can be configured to be the single entry point, check code is cheap to write with AI, and models extract invoice lines reliably enough when totals are checked.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the contract register and budgets current enough for checks to mean something; agency rate disputes.
tasks.human_edge: Signing rights and judgement on unusual payments; spotting a pressure or fraud pattern a rule does not describe.

ambition.what: A pre-payment gate: no Rabobank batch is released unless every line passed the checks or has a signed exception

tasks.altitude: The controller sees only exceptions and large amounts, about a third of today's checking time, and gains a clear exception log for the auditor.

reach.learn: Which coding errors cause false exceptions
How agency worker records link to hours and rates

evidence.claim: AFAS bank matching runs on fixed rules on reference, IBAN and invoice number
Nothing posts until bank, AR and AP tie out; the model drafts and the tie-out decides
Cash allocation needs mandatory human review and approval with logs

assumptions: Most purchase invoices already run through an AFAS workflow
A contract register with agreed rates exists or can be built
Agency worker names in invoices are personal data; processing stays within existing AVG purposes
unknowns: Share of payment requests that arrive outside AFAS today
Whether all three agencies can send UBL or a structured export
Current approval thresholds and dual-signing rules in Rabobank
research_questions: On three months of history, how many invoices would the checks pass without touch?
How many duplicate or IBAN-change cases occurred in the past two years?
Can AFAS store a check flag on the invoice via UpdateConnector so the workflow can route on it?
